calls.reason: The packet has no record either confirming or ruling out a $150B arrangement. The ITPro report on Sacks rejecting an AI bailout predates the claim, and the contract says a failed search cannot rule out a secret deal.

Cited figures show acceleration, not slowdown: run rate went from about $25B in March to $40B by mid-August. CNBC reported 20% month-over-month growth in July, and the CFO said enterprise grew faster than expected.
OpenAI has not gone public; per TechCrunch, Altman ruled out a 2026 IPO. With no completed offering, there is nothing to test the stated requirement against.
The year-end deadline has not passed. Ramp's panel shows slower spending growth but also an October peak, and it does not measure either firm's total revenue or show that token-maxxing has ended.
This is an open-ended every-year forecast, and no full year of financing needs has been recorded since the claim. The reported $30B bridge-round talks are early and do not cap annual needs.
The condition, Oracle losing OpenAI revenue, has not happened. Oracle announced an expanded OpenAI partnership on October 27, 2026, so the conditional cannot be tested.
